subject: Agentized telemetry adaptor proposal — LangChain & LlamaIndex
messages:
From: Oliver Greene <oliver@llamalabs.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Partnerships <Partnerships@promptsmith.ai>
Date: 2026-04-19T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Lightweight 'agentized' telemetry adaptor idea for LlamaIndex + LangChain

Hi Hannah —

Thanks again for the product call earlier. Quick follow-up: PromptSmith and LlamaLabs have been experimenting with a lightweight agent wrapper that surfaces tool calls, prompt templates, and step-level latencies in a small JSON trace (we call it "agent-trace-v1"). We think this could be a low-friction way for Redwood to consume higher-fidelity telemetry from LangChain / LlamaIndex integrations without forcing customers to install heavyweight tracing stacks.

Would Redwood be interested in an adaptor we can bake that emits agent-trace-v1 to Redwood's ingestion endpoint? High-level idea:
- A tiny shim in the SDK that emits ordered call events (prompt, tool-invocation, return)
- Minimal sampling (1-5%) plus batch upload to reduce cost
- Optional token-level timing when available

We'd love to draft a short SOW and a sample trace format and run a small pilot with 2 customers (one LangChain-heavy, one LlamaIndex-heavy). I copied PromptSmith partnerships since they're the pilot anchor.

If you're open, can we set a 45-min technical sync next week?

Thanks —
Oliver
Principal Engineer, LlamaLabs

Subject: Re: Lightweight 'agentized' telemetry adaptor idea for LlamaIndex + LangChain

Oliver —

Appreciate the note and the attachment. This aligns well with Redwood Optimize's goal to recover signal without adding inference overhead for customers. Quick answers: yes, we are interested; yes to a short SOW and a pilot.

Marissa, Karthik, Ben — looping you in to scope the technical and product requirements. High-level asks from our side:
- Minimal runtime overhead target: <5% p99 CPU for the adaptor
- Support for both LangChain and LlamaIndex call models (agent loops, retriever flows)
- Clear mapping from agent events -> Redwood trace schema (events, token counts, durations)

Oliver, can you share a sample trace (schema + 2 real example traces) and the pilot customer names? We're free for a 45-min sync on Wed 4/21 afternoon PT.

Thanks,
Hannah
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference

On Wed, Apr 21, 2026 at 09:00 AM Oliver Greene <oliver@llamalabs.com> wrote:
> Hi all — attaching two sample traces and a one-pager for the adaptor.

Thanks for the samples, Oliver — looked through both. Two quick technical notes from the runtime/instrumentation side:

1) Batching/ingest: we'll want the adaptor to emit batched payloads and include a compact checkpoint (last_event_id) so retries are idempotent. We can accept newline-delimited JSON (NDJSON) uploads to the ingestion endpoint (details in the SOW draft).

2) Token-level timings: great to have but we need a schema hook to indicate whether timings are precise (measured) vs. estimated. Please add a boolean field in the schema (timing_precision: measured|estimated).

Pilot scope proposal (30 days):
- Week 1: integration prototype for LangChain (agent loop) + LlamaIndex retriever wrapper
- Week 2: instrumentation hardening (idempotency, sample config) + internal perf test against p99 target
- Week 3: customer pilot onboarding (PromptSmith Labs + one Redwood internal test account)
- Week 4: roll-up report + SOW for GA readiness

I've attached a very rough SOW draft (SOW-draft-agent-adaptor.docx) and a quick KPI matrix (redwood-sample-kpi-matrix.csv). Oliver/Emma — can you confirm resource commitments (1 eng + 0.5 PM from your side) and the expected public repo/OSS licensing for the adaptor?

- Marissa
Senior Product Manager, Redwood Inference
